content: The Court of Reggio Calabria issued a non-final judgment regarding a property release claim following a divorce. The plaintiff asserted exclusive ownership of the apartment via a 1993 deed of gift, seeking the eviction of her former husband. The court qualified the claim as a personal action for restitution, distinguishing it from an action for recovery (rivendicazione) and its associated probatio diabolica. Since the couple's children were financially independent, no judicial assignment of the marital home was granted to the defendant. Consequently, the defendant was characterized as an occupant without title, as his right of use expired alongside the marital bond. The court reaffirmed that exclusive property rights prevail immediately when the social and legal justification for cohabitation dissolves. The defendant’s counterclaims for reimbursement of construction costs and furniture division did not grant a right of retention. The judge ordered the vacating of the premises within 45 days, removing all personal effects. Financial disputes regarding the property's increased value were deferred to a subsequent evidentiary stage. This ruling ensures the owner's immediate recovery of the asset despite pending cross-claims for credits.
